title: Fix floating billing artifacts from interleaved streaming sessions across deployments
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent extra token/charge line items after using streaming endpoints across Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Problem surfaces when a single logical streaming session is split into rapid interleaved substreams (resume/append/retry) across routing boundaries; the billing pipeline creates duplicated ledger rows that survive downstream aggregation and result in visible overcharges. This ticket tracks triage, patch, rollback/credits, and release of a durable fix.
impact_summary: High customer impact: 3 enterprise customers reported visible overcharges (non-duplicative application traffic). Estimated to affect <1% of streaming sessions but can generate 2x token counts for affected sessions. Potential revenue and CS escalations if not fixed quickly.
reproduction_steps: Open a streaming generation against hosted API with short-lived intermittent network interruptions
Client attempts resume semantics with new substream connections within 2s window
Traffic routed across two Dedicated pools during failover simulation
Observe ingest-layer creating two ledger entries for same logical sequence (different substream_id), downstream aggregator fails to dedupe because canonical session_id mismatch
Run billing aggregation query on staging dashboard to reproduce duplicate-line growth
root_cause_analysis: The ingest aggregator uses (tenant_id, session_token) as the canonical key for deduping streaming chunks. When substreams are resumed quickly, a new ephemeral substream_id is generated by the proxy and the session_token is briefly inconsistent across routing boundaries due to a stale cache TTL. Two independent write paths commit ledger rows before the aggregator's dedupe window expires. Additionally, the downstream billing merge job relies on a non-idempotent append that uses arrival timestamp as a tie-breaker, making it impossible to reconcile duplicates post-hoc.
mitigation_actions: Applied temporary billing hold & disabled auto-finalize for affected tenants (support action) to prevent invoice generation
Issued manual credits for the three highest-impact customers as immediate remediation
Added observability alert (billing.duplicate-lines.rate) to trigger on >0.5% duplicate rate per tenant
Deployed a feature-flagged patch to make streaming chunk writes idempotent (use stream_block_id derived from kernel sequence + tenant checksum)
proposed_fix: Canonicalize stream identity at the edge: ensure proxy attaches a persistent canonical_session_id to all substreams within 30s of initial stream creation. Update ingest pipeline to use (tenant_id, canonical_session_id, stream_block_id) for dedupe. Change billing merge job to use stable idempotency keys rather than timestamps. Add regression unit + integration tests exercising interleaved resume scenarios.
rollout_plan: 1) Release patch behind feature flag to staging and run synthetic interleaved-resume test harness; 2) Canary to 5% of production tenants (no billing finalization) for 24h, monitor duplicate-lines.rate and per-tenant token deltas; 3) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with automated rollback if duplicate rate rises above baseline+0.2% or if tail-latency increases >10%.
